Looking at this question about phylloxera (Daktulosphaira vitifoliae) chromosome morphology, I need to recall what is known about the karyotype of this insect.

Phylloxera is a Hymenopteran that uses haplodiploid sex determination (females are XX, males are XO). In cytogenetic studies of phylloxera, the X chromosome has been characterized as being the longest chromosome in the karyotype when compared to the autosomal chromosomes. This is a notable feature of the phylloxera karyotype that distinguishes it from some other insects where the X may be of intermediate or shorter length.

[ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
